tools.name: create_context
tools.description: Share text, markdown, code, or HTML as an auto-expiring ctxt.io link. For visual output (styled reports, tables, charts, diagrams) prefer format=html with self-contained HTML: inline CSS and inline SVG render fully; <script> is stripped server-side and JavaScript never runs, so keep it static. Free

tools.name: read_context
tools.description: Fetch the content of an existing ctxt.io link. Accepts a full ctxt.io URL, a /3/<code> path, or a bare code. Password-protected links need the password argument.

tools.name: delete_context
tools.description: Delete a ctxt.io link you created. Requires the delete_token returned by create_context. Immediately removes public access and requests backing-storage deletion. Destructive and not undoable — confirm with the user before calling.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_context" references sensitive artifacts (password). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "delete_context" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Delete a ctxt.io link you created. Requires the delete_token returned by create_context. Immediately removes public access and requests backing-storage deletion…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_context, read_context · Private data: create_context, read_context · Public sink: create_context · Destructive: create_context, delete_context.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_context, read_context · Private data: create_context, read_context · Public sink: create_context · Destructive: create_context, delete_context

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
